summary: The change is exactly the surgical rewrite task 01 asked for: printDataCell binds the cell value to a local, truncates the local and prints the local, leaving the result set read-only. Verified in an isolated HEAD+diff worktree — go vet clean, gofmt clean, all render tests pass, and both new tests genuinely fail against the pre-change implementation, so they are real regression guards rather than tautologies. Byte-identity of rendered output holds by construction (the error-path ordering, the strictly-greater comparison, the width-1 cut plus '~' and the %-*s padding are preserved verbatim), and the doc comment's factual claim about calculateDelta was checked against internal/stat/postgres.go:596. Only minor, optional suggestions remain.

suggestions.suggestion: The `width <= 0` branch (returns `fmt.Errorf("zero or negative width, skip")` and prints nothing) has no direct test in top/stat_test.go — grep finds only comments referencing that error text, never an assertion on it. Acceptance criterion 3 of the task ('the zero/negative-width branch still returns an error and prints nothing') is therefore verified by code reading alone. Since the task touched this function, a five-line test would pin it: build a config whose ColsWidth[0] <= 0, seed a non-empty value (the branch is only reachable when len(value) > width, so an empty cell never enters it), call printDataCell/printStatData and assert both the error and an empty bytes.Buffer.
suggestions.benefit: Turns the last unverified acceptance criterion into an executable guard and pins the exact error text, which task 03 (frame store) and task 09 will render through repeatedly.

suggestions.suggestion: Both new tests are named Test_printDataCell_* but neither calls printDataCell — they drive it through printStatData + visibleColumns. The names were prescribed verbatim by the task's TDD Anchor, so this is not a deviation, and testing through the public render entry point is arguably the better level (it also covers the frozen-column call site). Worth a one-line note in the test comment that the function under test is reached via printStatData, or renaming to Test_printStatData_* if the task's naming is not load-bearing for downstream tasks.
suggestions.benefit: A reader grepping for printDataCell coverage is not misled about the level at which the behaviour is pinned.

suggestions.suggestion: Test_printDataCell_widenAfterTruncation asserts only Contains("abcdefghij") on the wide render. Adding NotContains("abcd~") would make the intent explicit rather than implicit (today a hypothetical render that printed BOTH the full value and a stale truncated one somewhere in the row would still pass). Low value — the current assertion is sufficient for the stated property — but it costs one line.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the 'the truncated form is gone, not merely accompanied by the full value' intent explicit for future editors of the render path.

verification.method: Isolated git worktree at HEAD with only task01.diff applied, so the parallel task-02 work in the working tree (top/pause.go, top/pause_test.go, top/ui.go, top/ui_test.go, top/config.go, top/keybindings.go) could not affect the result. Worktree removed afterwards; the user's working tree was not modified.
results: gofmt -l top/stat.go top/stat_test.go — no output (both formatted)
go test ./top/ -run 'printDataCell|printStatData' -v — 5 tests, all PASS, including Test_printStatData_truncation unmodified
go test ./top/ -run 'render|visibleColumns|printStat|Test_print' — ok, no regressions in the wider render suite

Negative control: with top/stat.go reverted to HEAD and the new tests kept, BOTH new tests FAIL (doesNotMutateSource: expected 'abcdefghij', actual 'abcd~'; widenAfterTruncation: wide render still shows 'abcd~'). The tests are genuine regression guards.

AC1 grep: `grep -rn 'Result\.Values\[' top/ --include='*.go' | grep -v _test.go` returns exactly two hits (top/stat.go:1054 filter match, top/stat.go:1111 the new local read) — both reads. No assignment into any field of s.Result remains in non-test code.

Byte-identity reasoning: the truncation condition stays strictly-greater, the width<=0 check stays INSIDE the overflow branch (so a short value in a zero-width column behaves as before), the cut is still byte-based value[:width-1]+"~", and the padding is still %-*s with ColsWidth[i]+2. visibleColumns returns a window over scrollable columns starting at index 1 (`first: 1` in the degenerate case), so column 0 is never printed twice within one render; even if it were, old and new produce identical bytes for a re-printed cell.
Doc-comment fact check: internal/stat/postgres.go:590-597 confirms `delta = curr` when interval == [2]int{0,0} — the comment's aliasing rationale is accurate, not a plausible-sounding invention.

dimensionNotes.architecture: Restores the printer's contract (format, do not mutate). Matches patterns.md 'Testable TUI Rendering' — printers take io.Writer, tests assert against bytes.Buffer. No signature change, no deep copy (Decision 10's rejected alternative correctly avoided).
dimensionNotes.errorHandling: Unchanged error path, still returned before any slicing and before any write to w. No swallowed errors; printStatData still propagates.
dimensionNotes.crossFileConsistency: printDataCell's two call sites in printStatData (frozen column 0 and the windowed loop) are untouched and still pass the absolute column index. stat.Stat / stat.PGresult field usage matches internal/stat definitions. No import or signature drift.
dimensionNotes.security: No new input handling; the [029] value-sanitisation debt is untouched as the task required. Removing the write also removes the only mutation of a values array that, for DiffIntvl == [0,0] views (including the default `activity` screen), is shared with the collector's own snapshot.
dimensionNotes.performance: Neutral. One string header copy into a local; the truncation still allocates the same single concatenated string, and only on the overflow path.
dimensionNotes.scopeDiscipline: Diff is 5 changed lines in stat.go plus a doc-comment block and 44 added test lines. No neighbouring function reformatted, no existing test edited or relaxed (confirmed: the diff against stat_test.go is additions only).
